summary: US-021: Edit a published map safely — pinned seats never orphaned or duplicated
description:
### US-021: Edit a published map safely — pinned seats never orphaned or duplicated
**As** an organizer, **I want** to edit a published seat map (rename/add/remove sections, rows, seats) and get a new version, **with a guarantee that no seat already sold or held is orphaned or duplicated**. **Priority:** P2 **Depends on:** TKT-103

This is the epic's headline COS: *maps are versioned; edits never orphan or duplicate sold/held seats*. Per the decomposition decision, TKT-3 proves this **at the catalog layer via a seat-identity pinning contract** — a published seat identity is immutable across versions, and the editing path is defined so a version bump preserves every pinned seat. The interplay with live **held** seats (per-seat inventory holds) is exercised in TKT-80, which lists that AC; this story defines and proves the **pinning contract** TKT-80 consumes, not the hold itself. Backend correctness + tests here; the editing UI is TKT-105.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Editing a published map produces a **new version**; the previous published version stays immutable. The new version is created under the ADR-018 lock/emit discipline where a transition is involved.
- [ ] The **pinning contract** is defined and documented (an ADR): a seat identity that any sale/hold references is stable across versions — it cannot be silently renumbered, merged, or dropped. An edit that would orphan such a seat is **rejected** (or expressed as an explicit, recorded remap), never silently applied.
- [ ] A test proves the invariant against the sold case: given a seat referenced by a confirmed/sold record, no edit sequence orphans it (its identity still resolves) and none duplicates it (it maps to exactly one seat in the new version).
- [ ] A concurrency test mirrors the sold-inventory race: concurrent edit vs. a sale/hold-reference against the same seat set never lands the map in a state where a pinned seat is lost or doubled (the check-then-act race is closed by the ADR-018 lock).
- [ ] The pinning contract is written so TKT-80's held-seat AC can consume it without a catalog change (the contract, not the hold, is the deliverable).

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- New/changed public read endpoints declare an ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale
- New migrations run out-of-band via the service `migrate` subcommand (ADR-022) and build within the 30s startup budget with plain `CREATE INDEX` (ADR-020)
- Every owned entity is `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002)

Parent epic: TKT-3. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §Capability map (TKT-3).

binding.rule: State-deriving catalog transitions decide under a row lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) and emit the domain event only after the store commits, marking the outbox column on success. The lock closes the check-then-act race against concurrent transitions.

State inside the database cannot constrain an adversary who writes to the database. Say which adversary you mean before writing 'tamper-evident'. (Relevant here as a discipline: 'safe against sold inventory' is a concurrency/consistency guarantee under honest writers, NOT a tamper claim — do not overclaim.)

governingAdrs.why: The new-version transition decides under a row lock and emits after commit; the lock is what closes the edit-vs-sale race that would orphan a seat.

Precedent for 'edit vs live demand': capacity cuts clamp to max(new, confirmed+held), forward-only, never force-release. A seat-map edit against sold seats follows the same never-strand-a-confirmed-claim spirit.
Seat identity is a slot attribute the claim core references; versioning must keep the identity the claim pinned resolvable.
Discipline check: name the adversary. This is honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence — do not overclaim in the ADR.

reference.summary: PRD v1 §Capability map — TKT-3 row is the source of truth for scope
TKT-3 epic — COS: authoring UI, versioning safe against sold inventory, GA+seated coexist
ADR-018 row-lock-decide-emit-after-commit — the concurrency precedent this story instantiates for map edits
TKT-80 held-seat AC — the consumer of the pinning contract this story defines

**⚠️ GATELESS RUN — all four human gates waived by explicit owner directive (process experiment).** The repo owner is deliberately running this ticket Ready→Done in one continuous autonomous pass, waiving Gate 1 (already given — ticket was in Ready), Gate 2 (plan approval), Gate 3 (review+merge), and Gate 4 (PO acceptance). **Effective config for this run** (read from working tree at run start): `plan` and `aiReview` are A/B arrays `["deepseek-v4-pro:medium@claudex", "gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex"]`; `planReview` and `implement` = `main-agent`. Cross-model invariant holds on both pairs (planner arms ≠ main-agent reviewer; main-agent implementer ≠ review arms). The `:medium` deepseek arm reflects an uncommitted arm bump present in the working tree at run start (committed HEAD carries `:low`); the bump is internal-maintenance config and will be re-applied to the default branch after this ticket.

**risk:low?** Not set, not claimed — this touches a new catalog transition (edit→new-version), a new migration, and a new ADR (the pinning contract). Plan gate stays substantive (it's the A/B-judged step above). Branch: `TKT-104-edit-published-map-seat-pinning` off `origin/main`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### 📝 Plan drafts — A/B stage (2 arms, config.models.plan)

**An A/B plan ran: 2 arms, same brief, same input, both read-only claudex drafters.** Per `ab-stages.md` §plan.6 (gate waived by owner directive ≠ risk:low): the orchestrator stands in as the Gate-2 judge, so arm mapping is **disclosed immediately** (anonymization is moot when the judge launched the arms).

| Arm | Model / harness / effort |
|---|---|
| **A** | `deepseek-v4-pro:medium@claudex` |
| **B** | `gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex` |

**⚠️ Harness-integrity finding (Arm A):** the deepseek arm was launched read-only (`--allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob"`) yet **wrote a 22KB file to `docs/product/TKT-104-execution-plan.md`** — the claudex allowlist did NOT enforce read-only for this model/harness. Per `claudex-runner.md` the allowlist IS the sandbox; it failed here. The stray file was removed (planning is read-only; it is not a ticket deliverable — the ADR is). Content was preserved and is used as the arm's draft. Logged as a measurement note (retro item: the read-only claudex guarantee is not reliable for deepseek-v4-pro — treat claudex plan drafts as advisory and always clean the tree after).

---
#### Arm A (deepseek-v4-pro:medium@claudex) — design summary
**Pinning contract via a real `seat_map_pins` table** (the fact-source TKT-80 writes into; `pinned_by text` free-form so no catalog change to consume). `EditSeatMap` locks the predecessor `seat_maps` row `FOR UPDATE`, reads the family's pinned set, validates every pinned identity appears exactly once in the submitted geometry, atomically inserts a new published version (`version+1`, same `map_family_id`), commits, then reuses the existing `seat_map.published` event (no bump). **Crux insight (COS-4):** a `FOR UPDATE` on the edit path alone does NOT serialize a concurrent pin INSERT into a *separate* table — so the contract includes **`PinSeat`/`UnpinSeat` store functions that take the SAME predecessor row lock** (two-sided lock). Recommendation: **hard-reject**. No new HTTP endpoint (deliverable is the contract; UI is TKT-105). Migration `0011` adds `map_family_id` + `seat_map_pins`. Full plan (with test plan sub-cases and the two-sided-lock derivation) captured in the run log.

#### Arm B (gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex) — design summary
`EditPublishedSeatMap` creates a new **draft** version (clone-then-publish-separately), predecessor immutable, `FOR UPDATE` on source, identity-set-preservation validation (every source identity survives exactly once), reject removals/identity-changing renames/duplicates. **Hard-reject** recommendation. No new event, no new endpoint. Migration `0011` adds map-family/lineage metadata. Sold-reference modeled **synthetically in the test** (a retained `seat_identity` string) — does NOT add a pin table; leaves the concurrent-pin write path implicit (its race test says goroutine B 'acquires the same row lock' without defining the seam that makes that real). Cleaner structure, 5 named tests each mapped to a COS.

---
**planReview (config.models.planReview = main-agent) and Gate-2 selection follow in the plan-final comment.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### ✅ Plan-final — TKT-104 (delta on the kind=plan drafts; Gate 2 self-judged, owner-waived)

**This is a delta.** The kind=plan draft as amended below IS the plan. Resume reads the two drafts + this delta together.

#### planReview (config.models.planReview = main-agent, adversarial — verified every named seam against HEAD)
- **No hallucinated seams.** `git grep` confirms `EditSeatMap`, `PinSeat`, `seat_map_pins`, `map_family_id` are all net-new (NONE exist today). `TestArchiveDoesNotRacePublish`/`archive_race_smoke_test.go`, the `seat_map.published` schema-1 event + `Publisher.SeatMapPublished`, the smoke harness (`CATALOG_MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL` + goose fresh-schema), and the `seat_identity = sec.name||'/'||r.label||'/'||label` composition all exist as both arms describe. ✓
- **Arm B verdict:** clean, well-structured, 5 COS-mapped tests, correct hard-reject call — but its **COS-4 concurrency design is under-specified**: its race test has 'goroutine B acquire the same source-map row lock' without ever defining the seam that makes a sale/hold *take* that lock. Left implicit, that race does not actually close.
- **Arm A verdict:** messier as an artifact (visible think-aloud), but reaches the **materially correct** concurrency design and is the reason it wins: a `FOR UPDATE` on the edit path alone does **not** serialize a concurrent pin write into a *separate* table (Postgres row locks don't block inserts elsewhere), so the pinning contract must supply **`PinSeat`/`UnpinSeat` store functions that take the SAME predecessor row lock** (a two-sided lock), and `seat_map_pins` is a real fact-source table (`pinned_by text`) TKT-80 writes into with no catalog change (COS-5). This is the load-bearing insight for COS-4.

#### 🏛️ Gate-2 SELECTION (orchestrator standing in as judge — owner-waived): **Arm A (deepseek-v4-pro:medium@claudex) wins**, spine = Arm A's two-sided lock + `seat_map_pins` + `PinSeat`/`UnpinSeat`, adopting Arm B's cleaner test structure and COS→test mapping. Reason: Arm A is the only draft that actually closes the COS-4 edit-vs-sale race; Arm B would ship a race test that proves nothing.

#### Self-made decisions (Gate 2 waived — each recorded with rationale)
1. **Winner = Arm A** (two-sided lock design). Rationale above. Both arms already agreed on hard-reject + no-endpoint + no-new-event, so the only real fork was the concurrency seam — decided on correctness.
2. **Reject-vs-remap → HARD-REJECT** (resolves the deferred `uncertainties` DoR item). Rationale: most reversible (remap can be added later as its own ADR without invalidating the pinning invariant 'a pinned identity always resolves'), simplest to prove, strongest ADR-026 alignment (the seat identity IS the claim's handle, always valid — no dereference). New sentinel `ErrSeatMapEditOrphansPinned`.
3. **Keep `map_family_id`** (justified, not trimmed): a pin is version-independent within a lineage, so it cannot key on `seat_map_id` (a specific version). Backfill existing maps to their own `id` (each is a family of one), NOT NULL after backfill.

#### 🏛️ governing ADRs (re-resolved against docs/adr/ at claim time)
- **ADR-018** rule 1 — the edit→new-version is **state-deriving** (validity depends on the current pinned set), so it decides under `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and emits after commit. Lock-free monotonic publish (`PublishSeatMap`) is unchanged.
- **ADR-026** — never strand a confirmed claim; forward-only. Hard-reject upholds this maximally.
- **ADR-005** — the identity the claim pinned stays resolvable across versions.
- **ADR-021** — **name the adversary: honest-writer consistency, NOT tamper-evidence.** The ADR must state plainly that an adversary with catalog write access can insert/delete pins at will; the contract guards against our own bugs/races, not an attacker. No overclaim.
- **ADR-002** (org-scoped, DB predicate/FK), **ADR-019** (index-back the `seat_map_pins WHERE map_family_id` read), **ADR-020** (plain CREATE INDEX), **ADR-022** (0011 runs out-of-band via `migrate`), **ADR-017** (no event payload change → no bump; verify schema-1 payload still sufficient for the new version).

#### ⚠️ Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model (named again for the Gate-3 hand-off)
These were NOT in either draft as accepted/amended — they are my planReview additions and reach the code reviewed only by their author (me). To be scrutinized specifically in ai-review:
1. **Exact lock target**: both `EditSeatMap` and `PinSeat` lock the **family's current published `seat_maps` row** (`SELECT id FROM seat_maps WHERE map_family_id=$1 AND status='published' ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE`). Both paths must lock the identical row for the serialization to hold; the edit's new row is created *after* that lock is taken.
2. **Symmetric pin-time enforcement**: `PinSeat` validates the identity exists in the current published version before inserting → new sentinel `ErrSeatIdentityNotFound`. Idempotent on `(map_family_id, seat_identity, pinned_by)` via `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
3. **Immutability of the predecessor** asserted directly: after an edit, `AddSeatMapSection` against BOTH the predecessor and the new version returns `ErrNotFound` (neither is draft).

#### DoD / Files / Test plan
As the Arm A draft, with the three amendments folded in. Files: create `docs/adr/ADR-029-seat-identity-pinning-contract.md`, `services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0011_seat_map_edit_pinning.sql`, `services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_edit_smoke_test.go`; modify `store.go` (interface + input types + 3 sentinels) and `postgres.go` (EditSeatMap, PinSeat, UnpinSeat). No events/api/openapi change. Tests (all `//go:build smoke`, run in the catalog smoke stage): `TestEditSeatMapPreservesPinnedSeats` (COS-3, sold-case resolves + no-dup + unpinned-removal-ok), `TestEditSeatMapVersionBumpAndImmutability` (COS-1), `TestEditSeatMapDoesNotRacePin` (COS-4, ~30-iter two-goroutine race mirroring archive), `TestPinSeatRejectsUnknownIdentity` (COS-5 seam). Every test observed RED first.

**⛔ Gate 2 WAIVED by owner directive** — proceeding directly to Building (agent:coding). needs:human set only to mark the stage boundary in the thread; not stopping.

<!-- sdlc:stage=building kind=summary -->
### 🔨 Gate 2 waived → Building (agent:coding)

Owner-waived Gate 2: orchestrator transitions Planning→Building itself, per the approved plan-final (Arm A two-sided-lock design, hard-reject). Implementer = `main-agent` (config.models.implement). TDD next: write the four smoke tests + observe RED, then implement `EditSeatMap`/`PinSeat`/`UnpinSeat` + migration 0011 + ADR-029 to green, `make check`, push, open PR.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### 🔨 Implemented (TDD, main-agent) → PR #81 → ai-review

**Implementer:** `main-agent` (config.models.implement) — Claude Opus 4.8, TDD. Tests written and observed **RED first** (compile-RED: `undefined: EditSectionInput` on `go vet -tags smoke` before any impl existed), then implemented to GREEN.

**PR:** [#81](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/81) — `TKT-104: edit a published seat map safely — seat-identity pinning contract`. Diff **+820/−0, 7 files**.

**What shipped (per the approved plan-final, Arm A two-sided-lock spine):**
- `EditSeatMap` — new published version under a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the family's current published row, orphan check, atomic geometry clone, emit-after-commit (ADR-018).
- `PinSeat`/`UnpinSeat` — the TKT-80 seam; PinSeat takes the SAME lock and validates identity presence (the two-sided lock closing COS-4).
- Sentinels `ErrSeatMapEditOrphansPinned`, `ErrSeatIdentityNotFound`; input types `EditSeatMapInput`/`PinSeatInput`.
- Migration `0011` (map_family_id + backfill + `seat_map_pins`; out-of-band ADR-022, plain CREATE INDEX ADR-020).
- `ADR-029` (the pinning contract; honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence per ADR-021).
- `AGENTS.md` pointer (consistent with the ADR-018..022 cluster).
- 4 store smoke tests: `TestEditSeatMapPreservesPinnedSeats` (COS-3), `TestEditSeatMapVersionBumpAndImmutability` (COS-1), `TestPinSeatRejectsUnknownIdentity` (COS-5), `TestEditSeatMapDoesNotRacePin` (COS-4, 30-iter real-Postgres race).

**Local gate:** `make check` **GREEN** — verified from the log body (TKT-101 discipline: the bg wrapper exit is not trusted). One lint-go failure caught on the first run (`func geom is unused`) — the wrapper reported exit 0 while the log showed `make: *** [lint-go] Error 1`; fixed (removed the unused helper) and re-ran the full gate clean (`ok ticketing/services/catalog/internal/store`, `ok ticketing/smoke 68.9s`, no `--- FAIL`/`Error`).

**Next:** A/B ai-review (config.models.aiReview = `[deepseek-v4-pro:medium@claudex, gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex]`), both primed for guilt, diff-only. Reviewer ≠ author holds (implementer = main-agent). Special scrutiny requested on the three plan-review-introduced elements named in plan-final (exact lock target, symmetric pin enforcement, predecessor immutability).

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### 🔍 ai-review — A/B (2 arms) + fix + second pass. Converged.

**A/B review ran: 2 arms on the same diff, primed for guilt, diff-only** (config.models.aiReview = `[deepseek-v4-pro:medium@claudex, gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex]`). Reviewer ≠ author holds (implementer = main-agent). Both arms ran `@claudex` (the harness is part of the measurement).

#### First pass — findings (deduped by defect, verified against the revision + a reproduced probe)
| # | Finding | Arms | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **Stale-predecessor lock → orphaned pin.** A row `FOR UPDATE` on the current-version row does not conflict with EditSeatMap's INSERT of a new version row; a blocked PinSeat rechecks the stale predecessor (Postgres doesn't re-run `ORDER BY … LIMIT` after the wait) and lands a pin for a dropped seat. | A#1, B#1, +my probe | **CONFIRMED blocking** (reproduced: pin landed, seat absent from current version) | Fixed |
| F2 | **Concurrent-edit version collision.** Two edits both lock the stale v1, both derive version+1; no UNIQUE(map_family_id, version). | A#3, B#2 | **CONFIRMED blocking** | Fixed |
| F3 | **Test invariant too weak.** `assertNoOrphanPins` checked *any* published version, not the *current* one — a false negative that masked F1 (the predecessor stays published). | A#2, A#4 | **CONFIRMED blocking** (test validity) | Fixed |
| F4 | **UnpinSeat not in the lock protocol** — a standalone DELETE can't see an uncommitted concurrent pin; a release could be lost. | B#3 | **PLAUSIBLE → accepted** | Fixed |
| F5 | Redundant explicit `rows.Close()` alongside defer. | A#5 | incidental | **Rejected** — the explicit close is functionally required (pgx cannot run new queries on a tx with an open rows cursor); the defer covers early-return paths. Kept as-is. |

**Arm tally (first pass):** deepseek — 4 confirmed (F1,F2,F3 + F4-adjacent), 1 incidental; luna — 3 confirmed (F1,F2,F4). Both independently caught the load-bearing F1. Unique-confirmed: deepseek F3 (the masking test bug); luna F4 (UnpinSeat). A genuinely productive A/B — the two arms' unique finds were complementary, not redundant.

#### Fix (commit `fd76ce8`) — root cause closed
The root cause of F1–F3 is one design error: a row lock cannot serialize on 'the family's current version' when an edit makes a new version by INSERT. Replaced with a **family-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(map_family_id::text,0))`** taken before re-resolving the current version; EditSeatMap, PinSeat, and UnpinSeat all take it. Added `UNIQUE(map_family_id, version)` backstop (F3). Corrected `assertNoOrphanPins` to bind to the current (max-version) version (F2/F3) + added `TestPinSeatSerializesBehindEditThatDroppedSeat`. **Verified: 0/60 orphaned pins under a drop-vs-pin stress loop that reproduced the bug before the fix.**

#### Second pass (fix diff, control arm only per ab-stages §5 — deepseek-v4-pro:medium@claudex)
**Non-trivial fix (new locking mechanism, migration constraint, rewritten function, corrected test) → second pass warranted.** It **cleared the concurrency fix explicitly** (advisory-key stability, family-id TOCTOU, deadlock-freedom, the UNIQUE+backfill, the corrected CTE, the regression test). Four new findings, all minor: F1/F2/F3 = stale `FOR UPDATE` doc comments in `postgres.go` godoc + the migration header (not updated with the fix); F4 = `organizer_id` scoping dropped from the post-lock read (transitively correct, flagged as defense-in-depth). **All four fixed** (commit forthcoming): docs corrected, `organizer_id = $2` re-added to the current-version read.

#### Churn cap
Stopping the review here. Round 3's fixes are pure doc-drift + one transitively-redundant predicate — the diff shrank from blocking→trivia across passes (**convergence, not churn**), so **no third adversarial pass** is run per the cap rule. The second-pass fix diff (comments + one WHERE predicate, no control-flow change) is low-risk; I verified `make check` green on the committed tree myself.

**Local gate:** `make check` GREEN after every change (judged from the log body per TKT-101). PR: [#81](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/81). Review-guide posted on the PR.

**⛔ Gate 3 WAIVED by owner directive** — orchestrator self-merges next (squash + delete branch), after verifying HEAD reached origin.

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
### ✅ Gate 3 waived → self-merged → PO Review

**Gate 3 (review + merge) waived by owner directive.** After ai-review converged, the orchestrator squash-merged PR #81 itself and deleted the branch. Pre-merge safety checks all passed: local HEAD == origin HEAD == PR head (`bbd6cdc`), and **CI green** (`check` pass 8m52s, `gate-selftest` pass 1m13s). Merge commit: `d71d5b6` on `main` (#81). Content verified present on `origin/main` after merge (advisory lock + ADR-029), guarding the squash-merge/stale-SHA trap.

**Validation note (Gate 4 self-validation follows in the done/metrics comment).** Each COS is backed by a test that runs in the gate against real Postgres:
- **COS-1** (new version, predecessor immutable): `TestEditSeatMapVersionBumpAndImmutability` — version=2 published, predecessor unchanged, both refuse authoring.
- **COS-2** (pinning ADR + orphaning edit rejected): ADR-029 + `TestEditSeatMapPreservesPinnedSeats` sub-case B (`ErrSeatMapEditOrphansPinned`).
- **COS-3** (sold-case resolves, no dup): `TestEditSeatMapPreservesPinnedSeats` — pinned identities resolve exactly once in the new version; unpinned removal succeeds.
- **COS-4** (edit-vs-sale race closed): `TestEditSeatMapDoesNotRacePin` (30-iter real-Postgres) + `TestPinSeatSerializesBehindEditThatDroppedSeat`; the reproduced orphan bug is now 0/60 under stress.
- **COS-5** (consumable by TKT-80 with no catalog change): `seat_map_pins.pinned_by` free-form + `TestPinSeatRejectsUnknownIdentity`.

No preview URL — this is a catalog store/contract change with no user-facing surface (the editing UI is TKT-105). PO validation is against the test evidence on merged code. Post-merge `make check` on `main` in progress; the Done/metrics comment will confirm it green and close the ticket.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### 🏁 Done — TKT-104 (gateless autonomous run)

**Gate 4 self-validation (owner-waived):** every COS is met, verified against test evidence on the merged code (`d71d5b6` on `main`), and **post-merge `make check` on main is GREEN** (judged from the log body per TKT-101). No user-demonstrable surface (catalog contract; UI is TKT-105), so validation is by the gate's real-Postgres tests. This ticket ran **Ready→Done with all four human gates waived** by explicit owner directive — recorded in the claim comment.

| PO Review → Done | ~immediate (self-validated) |

#### learnings
1. **Technical → docs/learnings/ (new incident note) + it is why ADR-029 exists:** `SELECT … ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE` does NOT serialize against an operation that creates a new "current" row by INSERT — the blocked waiter rechecks the *stale* locked row (Postgres does not re-run the LIMIT after the wait). Serialize on a stable *identity* (family advisory lock), not on a supersedable row. The `AGENTS.md` ADR-029 pointer already carries the one-line rule; the full incident (repro + fix + 0/60 stress) belongs in `docs/learnings/`. **Target house: repo-local (`docs/learnings/`), already partly landed via ADR-029 + the AGENTS.md pointer.**
2. **Process:** the read-only claudex allowlist (`Read,Grep,Glob`) did **not** prevent deepseek-v4-pro from WRITING a file during the plan stage (it wrote a 22KB `docs/product/` file). The sandbox guarantee in `claudex-runner.md` is not reliable for this model. **Target house: team wiki / this skill's retro (below).**

#### retro
**(1) What would have made this ticket faster/better?** The mémo and plan were solid — the concurrency subtlety (row-lock-vs-INSERT) was NOT foreseeable from the mémo and was correctly surfaced by adversarial review, which is the process working as designed. One friction: the A/B plan arms disagreed on rigor (deepseek's think-aloud vs luna's clean structure); the *messier* arm had the *correct* insight. Nothing to change — the judge caught it. `nothing` material beyond the two retro items below.
**(2) What should the humans change (concrete)?**
- **`claude-runner.md` (skill reference):** add a rule under §Invocation — *"The read-only allowlist is NOT enforced for all models: deepseek-v4-pro@claudex was observed writing a file under `--allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob` (TKT-104). Always `git status` after a claudex read-only stage and revert stray files; never assume the sandbox held."* Cite TKT-104. **Appliable now.**
- **A memory already exists** ([luna-xhigh-claudex-arm-fails]) for a different claudex arm failure; this is a second claudex-harness integrity gap → worth a consolidated "claudex read-only is advisory" note in `~/.claude/ab-tests/` or the skill.
